after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given that $c\cdot d=11$, find the angle between $c=⟨2t,1⟩$ and $d=⟨2,3⟩.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
First, since $c\cdot d=11$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & =11 \\ 2t\cdot 2+1\cdot 3 & =11 \\ 4t+3 & =11 \\ 4t & =8 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =⟨2(2),1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $c$ and $d$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{c\cdot d}{|\,c\,||\,d\,|} \\  & =\frac{{c}_{x}{d}_{x}+{c}_{y}{d}_{y}}{\sqrt{{c}_{x}^{2}+{c}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{d}_{x}^{2}+{d}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{11}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{11}{\sqrt{17}\cdot \sqrt{13}} \\  & =\frac{11}{\sqrt{221}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{11}{\sqrt{221}})≈{42.27}^{∘}.
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find $∠BAC$ given the points $A(2,1,-1)$, $B(3,-2,2)$, and $C(-1,-2,1).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,1,-1⟩,\,b=⟨3,-2,2⟩,\,c=⟨-1,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14046481/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨3,-2,2⟩-⟨2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-3,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨-1,-2,1⟩-⟨2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,2⟩\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot (-3)+3\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{19}\cdot \sqrt{22}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{418}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{12}{\sqrt{418}})≈{54}^{∘}.
$$

EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points A, B, C are

a=⟨2,1,−1⟩,b=⟨3,−2,2⟩,c=⟨−1,−2,1⟩.

The triangle △ABC is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote ∠BAC=θ.

First, we find the components of AB→ and AC→:

AB→=b−a=⟨3,−2,2⟩−⟨2,1,−1⟩=⟨1,−3,3⟩AC→=c−a=⟨−1,−2,1⟩−⟨2,1,−1⟩=⟨−3,−3,2⟩.

Now, the cosine of the angle between AB→ and AC→ is

cos⁡θ=AB→⋅AC→|AB→||AC→|=1⋅(−3)+(−3)⋅(−3)+3⋅212+(−3)2+32(−3)2+(−3)2+22=1219⋅22=12418.

Hence, θ=arccos⁡(12418)≈54∘.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
content.problem: Find $∠BAC$ given the points $A(2,1,-1)$, $B(3,-2,2)$, and $C(-1,-2,1).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,1,-1⟩,\,b=⟨3,-2,2⟩,\,c=⟨-1,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14046481/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨3,-2,2⟩-⟨2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-3,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨-1,-2,1⟩-⟨2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,2⟩\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot (-3)+3\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{19}\cdot \sqrt{22}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{418}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{12}{\sqrt{418}})≈{54}^{∘}.
$$
